newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Sao Paulo debt deal impacts Brazil fed govt - paper.
newsitem.headline: Sao Paulo debt deal impacts Brazil fed govt - paper.

text.p: A top Finance Ministry official has admitted Brazil's fiscal accounts will feel the impact of a recent deal to renegotiate Sao Paulo state's debt deal with state bank Banespa, a local newspaper said.
But ministry Executive Secretary Pedro Parente did not say how much it would cost the federal government to alleviate the state's 20 billion-real debt to the bank.

Parente, in an interview with financial daily Gazeta Mercantil, said an estimate by the Getulio Vargas Foundation economist that the debt deal will cost the federal government 15 billion reais over 30 years is a "guess."
The estimate errs in assuming bonds issued in lieu of the state's debt will carry a 12 percent real annual interest rate over the debt's 30-year life, he was quoted as saying.
Parente said the repayment terms on debt paper to be issued to banks in payment of state debts will vary but the interest rate will not, according to Gazeta.
"It's clear that we're not going to place in this deal any paper that will yield more than what we're paying now," he was quoted as saying. "At most, it will be the same."
Separately, Parente said the government's goal is to post a primary surplus of 1.5 percent of Gross Domestic Product in 1997 after reaching 0.5 percent this year.
"If we achieve a primary surplus of 1.5 percent next year and two percent the year after, we will not only stabilize the internal debt but also reduce the stock a little," he said.
